name: LinkedIn
description: Post to LinkedIn as the signed-in member and read their basic profile: create and delete posts, register image uploads. Uses a member access token from the LinkedIn developer portal. Reading posts and company pages needs LinkedIn's approval of the app. 5 tools.
instructions:
## LinkedIn
This connector posts to LinkedIn as the member whose access token you paste, and reads that member's basic profile. Posts and images go through LinkedIn's versioned API at `https://api.linkedin.com/rest` with the header `LinkedIn-Version: 202609`; the profile comes from the OpenID Connect endpoint `https://api.linkedin.com/v2/userinfo`, which is not versioned.

**What LinkedIn allows.** LinkedIn's API is tightly gated. Without a review by LinkedIn an app gets two self-serve products: **Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect** (scopes `openid`, `profile`, `email`) and **Share on LinkedIn** (scope `w_member_social`: create and delete the member's own posts, upload images). Reading posts (`r_member_social`), posting for a company page (`w_organization_social`), and searching people or connections all need LinkedIn's approval of the app for the Community Management API. A token without those scopes cannot reach them, whatever the connector does.

**Setup.**
1. Create an app at https://www.linkedin.com/developers/apps. LinkedIn asks you to link it to a company page.
2. On the app's **Products** tab, add **Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect** and **Share on LinkedIn**.
3. Open https://www.linkedin.com/developers/tools/oauth, pick the app, tick `openid`, `profile`, `email` and `w_member_social`, and generate a token, signed in as the member you want to post as.
4. Paste the token into `LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN` and install. Tokens last 60 days; then generate a new one and update the variable.

**Posting.**
1. Call `linkedin_userinfo`. Its `sub` is the member id; the author URN is `urn:li:person:<sub>`.
2. Call `linkedin_create_post` with that `author` and the text in `commentary`. Visibility defaults to `PUBLIC` (or `CONNECTIONS` for the member's network only); the post goes to the main feed and is published at once, LinkedIn has no drafts here. LinkedIn answers 201 with an empty body: the new post's URN (`urn:li:share:...` or `urn:li:ugcPost:...`) is in the `x-restli-id` response header, which the tool returns with the result.
3. `linkedin_delete_post` takes that URN as it is, for example `urn:li:share:7123456789012345678`; the connector encodes it for the address. Deleting is idempotent.

**Images.** `linkedin_register_image_upload` with `{owner: 'urn:li:person:<sub>'}` returns an `uploadUrl` and an image URN (`urn:li:image:...`). The file itself has to be sent to `uploadUrl` with an HTTP PUT outside this connector. Then create the post with `content: {media: {id: '<image URN>'}}`.

**Links.** LinkedIn does not fetch a preview from the address, so a link post needs the details itself: `content: {article: {source: '<URL>', title: '<title>', description: '<optional>'}}`, with an uploaded image URN as `thumbnail` if you want a picture.

**Reading a post.** `linkedin_get_post` needs `r_member_social`, which LinkedIn grants to approved apps only. With the two self-serve products it answers 403, even for the member's own posts.

**Errors.** 401: the token expired or was revoked; generate a new one. 403 `ACCESS_DENIED`: the token lacks the scope for that call (see above). 400 `MISSING_FIELD` or `INVALID_URN_TYPE`: check that `author` is `urn:li:person:<sub>` and that `commentary` is not empty. 426 or a version error: LinkedIn retired the `LinkedIn-Version` the tools send (each version is supported for at least a year); update the connector from the catalog. 429: the daily limit per member and app; try again later.
prerequisites: A LinkedIn developer app with the self-serve products **Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect** and **Share on LinkedIn**, and a member access token for it with the scopes `openid profile email w_member_social`. Reading posts and company pages needs LinkedIn's approval of the app (Community Management API).

LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN.label: Access token
LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN.help: linkedin.com/developers/tools/oauth: pick your app, tick openid, profile, email and w_member_social, and generate a token. Tokens last 60 days.

tools.name: linkedin_userinfo
tools.description: Get the signed-in member's profile from the OpenID Connect userinfo endpoint: sub (the member id, used as urn:li:person:<sub>), name, given_name, family_name, picture, locale, and email and email_verified when the token has the email scope.

tools.name: linkedin_create_post
tools.description: Publish a post on the member's feed. Required: author (urn:li:person:<sub> from linkedin_userinfo) and commentary. Needs the w_member_social scope. The new post's URN comes back in the x-restli-id response header.

author.description: URN of the author: urn:li:person:<sub>, with sub from linkedin_userinfo.

commentary.description: The post text, up to 3000 characters. Mention or hashtag syntax follows LinkedIn's little text format.

visibility.description: PUBLIC (anyone) or CONNECTIONS (the member's network only).

distribution.description: Where the post appears. Leave it out for the main feed: {feedDistribution: 'MAIN_FEED', targetEntities: [], thirdPartyDistributionChannels: []}.

isReshareDisabledByAuthor.description: True to stop others from resharing the post.

content.description: Optional. An image: {media: {id: 'urn:li:image:...', altText: '...'}} after linkedin_register_image_upload and the PUT of the file. A link: {article: {source: 'https://...', title: '...', description: '...'}}; LinkedIn does not fetch the preview itself. Leave out for a text post.

tools.name: linkedin_get_post
tools.description: Get a post by its URN. Needs the r_member_social scope, which LinkedIn grants to approved apps only: with the self-serve products this answers 403, even for the member's own posts.

postUrn.description: The post URN as returned, e.g. urn:li:share:7123456789012345678 or urn:li:ugcPost:7123456789012345678. Not URL-encoded; the connector encodes it.

tools.name: linkedin_delete_post
tools.description: Delete a post the member authored. Needs the w_member_social scope. Deleting an already deleted post also succeeds (204).

postUrn.description: The post URN as returned by linkedin_create_post, e.g. urn:li:share:7123456789012345678. Not URL-encoded; the connector encodes it.

tools.name: linkedin_register_image_upload
tools.description: Step 1 of an image post: register the upload. Returns value.uploadUrl and value.image (urn:li:image:...). Send the file to uploadUrl with an HTTP PUT outside this connector, then pass the image URN in linkedin_create_post's content.media.id. Needs the w_member_social scope.
